citation.title: ECMO criteria for influenza A (H1N1)-associated ARDS: role of transpulmonary pressure

provenance.quote: We report patients with influenza A (H1N1)-associated ARDS referred to the Molinette Hospital (University of Turin) for ECMO
Throughout the period of data recording all patients were orotracheally intubated
referred to the Molinette Hospital (University of Turin) for ECMO

Esophageal pressure was used to (a) partition respiratory mechanics between lung and chest wall, (b) titrate positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) to target the upper physiological limit of PPLATL (25 cmH2O)
The significant (P = 0.0001) increase of PPLATRS ... was associated with (a) the increase in ERS ... and EL ... (b) the increase of stress index ... and (c) the reduction in PaCO2
Fourteen patients were referred for ECMO.
Prospective data collection of patients with influenza A (H1N1)-associated ARDS referred for ECMO

exclusion_criteria.value: Exclusion criteria for ECMO were (a) intracranial bleeding and other major contraindication to anticoagulation, (b) previous severe disability; poor prognosis because of the underlying malignancy, and (c) mechanical ventilation for longer than 7 days [18].

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: The study targeted an absolute end-inspiratory transpulmonary pressure of 25 cmH2O, computed via elastance partitioning (PPLATL = PPLATRS × EL/ERS). Timing unclear because patients were referred to the ECMO center; time from intubation not reported. Obesity mixed: mean BMI 33.2 in ECMO group, 28.7 in no-ECMO group.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: Not listed in studies/COHORTS.md; no suspected overlapping reports.
unclear_items: design.enrolment_start/end: Abstract states October 2009–January 2010, Methods states September 2009–January 2010. Used Methods.

outcomes: The paper reports both a between-group comparison (ECMO vs no-ECMO) and a within-group comparison (no-ECMO conventional vs higher PEEP). We recorded the within-group comparison as the intervention effect. The ECMO group baseline values are recorded in population.additional_baseline.
arms: The study's patient groups (ECMO vs no-ECMO) are not ventilation conditions, so they are not listed in arms[]. Baseline by arm uses these group labels.

mortality and ECMO requirement outcomes: Reported only as cohort-level counts (3 deaths, 7 ECMO), not per ventilation condition. Recorded with arm_label 'conventional_ventilation' as the initial condition for all patients.
intervention.balloon_calibration: Method not reported; esophageal pressure measurement described only by reference to [20].
adults_18_plus criterion: No explicit age criterion stated, but patients were adults (ages 24-70 in Table 3). Coded yes.
data_only_in_figure: Fig. 1: Study flow chart showing oxygenation index and PPLATL values for ECMO and no-ECMO groups; values also in text and Table 2.
extraction_flags.general_notes: This is a case series of 14 H1N1-ARDS patients referred for ECMO. Esophageal pressure was used to partition respiratory mechanics and guide PEEP to target an end-inspiratory transpulmonary pressure of 25 cmH2O in 7 patients with low PPLATL, avoiding ECMO.
